title: Operator Choreography: Policy-aware Tasklets for Safe Automated Remediation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current support automation surface exposes a variety of brittle, imperative runbooks that are hard to test, audit, and safely auto-execute. Oncall engineers manually triage more incidents than necessary because playbooks lack composable, policy-aware primitives and there is no safe simulation harness for new automated actions.

Goal: Build an "operator choreography" layer: a library of small, idempotent tasklets (policy-aware primitives) and a lightweight orchestration shim that allows playbooks-as-tasks to run in simulated and staged environments with RBAC gating, audit logs, and telemetry-driven rollback. The work should make it straightforward to convert existing runbook steps into reusable tasklets, support dry-run/sandbox execution, and provide production-safe automatic remediations behind guardrails.

Scope: PoC tasklet SDK (Go + Node), orchestration shim that wires tasklets into existing ops eventing, simulator CLI for local dev, canary rollout controller for automated remediations, KMS-backed credential fetch for sensitive actions, audit events sent to observability pipeline, and a template migration guide for migrating 10 high-value runbooks.

Non-goals: Replacing the full runbook platform; advanced stateful choreography across long-running multi-step human approvals (this will be handled later with the approvals service).

Design highlights / decisions:
- Tasklets are single-purpose, idempotent binaries/libraries that expose a small typed input schema (JSON Schema) and a machine-readable safety metadata block (required permissions, side-effect tags, estimated cost).
- Policy engine will evaluate safety metadata + current context (incidents, environment) to allow/deny automatic execution.
- Every auto-execution must support a dry-run mode that emits a simulated diff (what would change) and a validation hook to be run in the simulator.
- Integrations: ops-event bus (for triggers), admin-credential-service (for secrets), telemetry pipeline (for metrics and traces), and auditlog-store (for compliance).

Compatibility / migration: Provide a shim that wraps existing bash/python playbook steps as tasklets with a small adapter. Provide a migration checklist and automation to convert the top 10 recurring runbooks identified by frequency and impact.
acceptance_criteria: Tasklet SDK: publish Go module and Node package with example tasklet and docs
Simulator: CLI that can run playbook composed of tasklets in dry-run mode and assert no mutating calls
Canary controller: policy rule that allows automatic remediation on <=P1 incidents after 2 successful non-prod replays
Audit trail: all tasklet executions (dry-run and real) recorded to auditlog-store with correlation IDs
Security: secrets fetched via admin-credential-service using KMS key and never logged in plaintext
Migration: conversion guide plus automated converter applied to 10 runbooks in staging with test coverage

2026-02-25 - Jun Park: Spike complete. Prototype tasklet interface implemented in Go. Found that existing bash steps lack structured input; adding adapter layer to wrap environment variables into typed schema. Posting PR for early feedback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tasklets/pull/219

2026-03-02 - SRE Review (Priya Rao): SREs raised concern about uncontrolled concurrency when many incidents trigger the same tasklet. Decision: add per-tasklet concurrency limits and global rate limiter; include backoff and circuit-breaker metadata in safety block.

2026-03-05 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Suggest explicit requirement that tasklets never access plaintext secrets. Action: use admin-credential-service and require token-scoped ephemeral creds. Marked security_review_required=true
2026-03-09 - Design (Maria Chen): Reviewed simulator UX. Requested clear dry-run diffs and a visual timeline for canary replays. Follow-up task to prototype timeline in console-ux backlog.

2026-03-12 - Jun Park: Canary controller MVP merged into staging; running automated replays for three converted runbooks. Found an edge case where DB migration step needs explicit lock; adding 'requires-lock' flag to safety metadata.
